Job Description:
The Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) serves as the regulatory and developmental authority for the early childhood sector in Singapore, overseeing key aspects of children’s development below the age of 7 in early childhood development centres (i.e.  kindergartens and childcare centres). ECDA is jointly overseen by the Ministry of Education (MOE) and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and is hosted under MSF.

The Regulation and Licensing Division is responsible for setting the regulatory standards and framework to ensure that for early childhood development centres (ECDCs) meet the standards of care and education necessary for children’s development in their early years. We do this in accordance with the Early Childhood Development Centres (ECDC) Act and Regulations, and maintain an overview of whether these legislative levers continue to be relevant as the early childhood sector and Singapore’s societal needs evolve. This involves regular reviews of sector development plans, regulatory requirements and enforcement frameworks, assessments of ECDCs for licence issuance and renewals, investigations on incidents and public feedback, and taking enforcement actions for non-compliances. 
 •	At least 2-3 years’ experience in policy development, operations policy and/or legislative work preferred. 
•	Strong analytical and logical thinking capability, with an ability to conceptualise broad ideas yet also pay attention to details.
•	Strong in writing and possess an ability to communicate clearly and persuasively.
•	Systematic and manages timelines well; able to work independently in a fast-paced environment. 
•	Good team-player with well-rounded interpersonal skills to work across teams and with diverse stakeholders (public and private sector). 
 In this operations-policy role, you will be involved in legislative reviews, translating of broader policies and legislation into guidelines and parameters for operationalisation, and framing of public communications. You will also be required to work closely with the policy directorate in MSF and involved in broader sector development reviews led by the policy directorate.
You will be involved in the following key areas:
•	Review of Early Childhood Development Centres (ECDC) Act and Regulations to uplift the standards and quality of care in preschools in Singapore. This includes gap analyses to identify legislative changes that are required and analyses of operational implications of such reviews.
•	Review regulatory standards and operational policies to operationalise legislative levers. This includes engagements with preschool operators, government agencies and other stakeholders.
•	Conceptualise and launch public communications efforts to create buy-in on legislative/regulatory changes from various stakeholders (e.g., preschool operators, parents, broader public), and prepare communication materials to address queries on regulatory requirements and breaches. 
•	Assessment of new applications for ECDC licences.

Job Description:
The Centre for Climate Research Singapore (CCRS) is a division of the Meteorological Service Singapore (MSS). At CCRS, our mission is to advance scientific understanding of tropical climate variability and change and its associated weather systems affecting Singapore and the wider Southeast Asia region, so that the knowledge and expertise can benefit decision makers and the community. Our vision is to be a world leading centre in tropical climate and weather research focusing on the Southeast Asia region.

CCRS is offering an exciting job opportunity for a scientist with a strong background in AI/ML and its application to climate, as well as good knowledge of climate variability and change in the tropics with focus on Southeast Asia. As part of the Department of Climate Research (DCR), the Climate Projections and Extremes Branch (CPEB) focuses on climate processes relevant to Singapore and the Southeast Asian region and developing next generation high resolution regional climate change projections for its stakeholders.

A core component of the work is the application of AI/ML methods for climate and climate change time scales, especially as part of the new AI-based production of high-resolution regional climate change projections.

We are therefore seeking an experienced scientist with a strong background in the application of AI/ML in climate science as well as an understanding of climate variability and change (especially for tropical regions such as Southeast Asia).

The job might be for you if you possess the following:

  • PhD/MSc degree in computer science, physical sciences and research experience in application of AI in climate, atmospheric/oceanic science, or meteorology
  • High proficiency in scientific computing, especially PYTHON, with experience applying AI/ML libraries

To manage the engagement of resident jobseekers and coordinate onboarding of community employers to the Jobs Nearby @ CDC scheme, connecting residents through localised workforce development and job matching initiatives.

Other ad-hoc duties not covered under main responsibilities and duties.

Knowledge & Skills

  • Knowledge in outreach, career and skills advisory, community engagement, HR/recruitment, or workforce development.

  • Knowledge of 2nd language (e.g. Mandarin, Malay, Tamil or dialects) to effectively engage with diverse residents in the community.

  • Good interpersonal communication skills and able to handle employer / jobseeker enquiries with basic knowledge of job market trends, workforce policies, etc.

  • Ability to work independently across different community locations and open to frequent travel within the district.

  • Flexibility to work  evenings, weekends and public holidays when required

  • Ability to conduct outdoor engagement activities and community outreach.

  • Proactive, persuasive and resourceful.

Key duties and responsibilities that need to be performed to meet the primary objective of the job.  This will include the important result areas (what) along with the rationale (why).

  • Manage the engagement of resident jobseekers and coordinate onboarding of community employers to the Jobs Nearby @ CDC scheme across CDCs and CCs.

  • Provide personalised guidance to resident jobseekers (e.g. listen with empathy, understand challenges, and guide jobseekers step-by-step in their job search journey).

  • Coordinate with employers (e.g. SMEs, neighbourhood businesses, community-based employers) and vendors to facilitate job seeker profiles creation, posting listings management, and effective utilisation of the job portal.

  • Guide jobseekers in setting up digital profiles, uploading documents, and navigating job portals or related platforms to apply for jobs.

  • Facilitate connections between jobseekers and employers through face-to-face or online platforms, including on-the-spot interviews.

  • Monitor jobseekers’ progress and outcomes, conduct regular follow-ups, and review service delivery processes (e.g. post-interview, post-placement, etc) to continuously improve the experience for both jobseekers and employers.

  • Expand employer networks and build relationships to strengthen engagement.

  • Organise and participate in events such as job fairs, learning festivals, and outreach activities to link jobseekers with employers.

  • Track and report data on jobseeker registrations, employer sign-ups, and success stories for monitoring and evaluation.

  • Provide operational guidance to new Job Ambassadors during onboarding to ensure familiarity with daily operations

1. Job Purpose

To support PA’s objectives to promote social cohesion and community bonding by creating conducive community spaces for people to meet, interact and bond.

Manage planning and design of new and upgrading community club/centre projects including other PA development projects to meet PA’s objectives, functional requirements and create conducive community spaces for residents to meet and bond to build social capital.   • Work with PA's expertise groups and CO for design innovation to CC facilities
  • Identify potentials & areas to further synergise with co-locators through formulation of design brief and areas of co-programming

  • Review designs of building projects and ensure quality in building designs
  • Drive the Community Workgroups on Design Briefs for new and upgrading of CCs
  • Proposed concept design for minor projects
  • Review interior design proposals with consultants and GRLs
  • Drive construction productivity

As Senior Manager (Creative Productions), serves as the Assistant Artistic Director to assist the Artistic Director to oversee all aspects of the artistic production of the Chingay Parade. The incumbent also serves as a choreographer and trainer for PA major arts and cultural events such as the Chingay Parade, PA Talents Community Outreach showcase/Concerts and National Day Celebration events. Additionally, the incumbent will also provide creative direction for PassionArts Festival, creating greater synergy between Chingay and PAssionArts, while planning and supervising all performances to meet the required artistic standards and to align with PA’s mission and objectives.

NA

  • Serves as the Assistant Artistic Producer, choreographer and trainer for the Chingay Parade to support in the conceptualisation of the parade concept and present interesting and spectacular items for the Parade.
  • Plans and coordinates future Chingay Parades to facilitate early engagement of partners and various communities.
  • Provides artistic advice/inputs and works closely with choreographers on Chingay and other arts and cultural performances to ensure that the outcomes achieve good standard of performance.
  • Works closely with the appointed music director/personnel to create, source and curate the selection of music to enhance the presentation of the performances at Chingay Parade and any other cultural performances presented by the PA Talents Dance Ensembles (PA Talents).
  • Provides artistic concept and supervises the production process (includes floats, costumes, props, sets) of Chingay and all other cultural activities/performances by PA Talents.
  • Conducts component, combined and full dressed rehearsals for Chingay.
  • Prepares cue sheets for the full-dress rehearsals and shows (including cues for performers, lightings, effects, singers) and serves as the cue master for the rehearsals and shows.
  • Serves as a production manager to Chingay performing groups, coordinating the groups’ participation in the Chingay Parade and its rehearsals and related fringe activities by providing administrative and technical support (choreography, training, costumes, floats, props, sound and lighting) to ensure their performances meet the acceptable standard of the parade.
  • Serves as a Relationship Manager to build and maintain close working relationships with partners and stakeholders to ensure successful delivery of PA's arts and cultural events.
  • Provides creative direction for the annual PassionArts Festival and ensure synergy between Chingay and PAssionArts.
  • Performs other duties as assigned by Senior Officers.
